summary: Both halves inspected. The torsor W(X)(1) has the stated universal property, and a base point splits the augmentation extension. The lower exact triangle reverses the arrangement used on p510 and the pointed conclusion is strengthened to a direct-sum isomorphism. Only the tilde strokes over the typed W/H/LH are handwritten, so broad hand markup is narrowed accordingly. Every display arrow and the triangle arrows are pen. The stray x strings in the prose are replaced by identifiable cancelled text or explicit doubt.

edits.reason: The W glyphs are typed and only their tildes are drawn by hand; narrow the provenance marking accordingly.
The H glyphs are typewriter text with a hand-added tilde; do not color the entire H as handwriting.
The displayed LH is typed and the tilde alone is pen.
The readable cancelled fragment is the funct; the intervening x is part of the typewriter strike.
The extra cancelled character after we is a readable typed r.
The extra dark cancelled character within triangle resembles g, but the overprint prevents certainty; literal x was cancellation markup.
The small pen-blotted character before weak is not securely recoverable as w; add explicit doubt.
Nonprinting convention records the hand-drawn triangle arrows.

notes.1: All W, H and LH letter forms under tildes are typed; markup now colors only the accent. The explicitly handwritten composition insertion remains hand text.
notes.2: The tiny marks around the o of Hot in the beta display are visible but do not yield a secure additional letter or symbol; they remain an observation rather than invented notation.
notes.3: The Z in the pointing map has a heavy underline with a small blot below its end; a second distinct underline cannot be established.
notes.4: The b of subobject retains serif typewriter form. The short accent-like stroke above it does not establish a separately added hand letter.
notes.5: All three triangle arrows, including both diagonals, are pen-drawn; their directions are unchanged.
notes.6: The pencil70 at bottom left is archival pagination; the typed page is512.
